name: Typing, translation and attestation centres

problems.words: Customers wait an hour at the counter and walk out
quick_ideas: Note arrivals by hour for a few days, so you see when the real peak is
Move one staff member's break away from that peak, so the queue is shorter when it matters.

workzap_build.text: a token and queue system with estimated wait times on a screen and on WhatsApp, plus a daily view of waits by hour.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many customers or jobs do you handle in a day?
problems.free_stops: the queue setup and staffing view are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many customers leave the queue before reaching the counter each busy period, so lost walk-ins are sized properly.
Give one staff member the job of watching and moving waiting files before peak hours, so the counter keeps flowing when lines build.

problems.words: People keep calling to ask if their documents are ready
quick_ideas: Tell every customer once, at the counter, when to expect their job back, so calls drop
Message the customers whose jobs are ready today, so they come in without calling.

workzap_build.text: a job tracker by reference number with automatic WhatsApp updates, with the customer's permission, when a job changes stage or is ready.

problems.free_stops: which stages send updates is worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many readiness calls come before noon and after noon for a few days, so the busiest checking time is clear.
Give one person a fixed time to review ready jobs and update the list, so callers get fewer mixed answers from staff.

problems.words: Original documents get misplaced in the office
quick_ideas: Do one check of every original currently in the office against open jobs, so you know what's where
Give originals one fixed shelf by job reference, so they stop wandering.

workzap_build.text: a document custody log showing which originals are in the office, which shelf, and who took them out and when.

problems.free_stops: the custody routine is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note where each original was actually found during one office walk round, so the main misplacement spots become obvious.
Give one person the job of returning every original to the same shelf before closing, so papers stop drifting between desks.

problems.words: We gave a customer someone else's documents once
quick_ideas: Agree that every handover is checked against the job reference by a second person, so mix-ups are caught
Review how the last mix-up happened once, so the gap is closed.

workzap_build.text: handover recorded against each job reference, so documents can only be marked collected for the matching job.

problems.free_stops: the handover check is designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note every handover correction or near-miss this week at the counter, so the risky moment in the routine stands out.
Make one person own the final handover check at every shift, so document releases stay consistent across the counter team.

problems.words: Courier pouches to the embassy go missing or get delayed
quick_ideas: List every pouch currently out with its send date, so overdue ones show
Chase the oldest this week, so they come back.

workzap_build.text: a courier and dispatch tracker with expected return dates, flagging pouches sent but not received.

problems.free_stops: the return rules and alerts are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the sent-out pouch notebook with what has returned once, so missing or slow pouches are spotted earlier.
Give one staff member the daily pouch follow-up call slot and notebook, so delayed returns are chased by one owner.

problems.words: Translations come back late from freelancers
quick_ideas: Give each freelancer a written due time with every job, so lateness is measurable
Note who was late this month, so you know who to rely on.

workzap_build.text: a translator assignment board with deadlines, reminders and on-time records per translator.

problems.free_stops: assignment and reminder rules are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare promised return times against actual arrival times for each freelancer this week, so the most reliable translators are clearer.
Give one person the job of logging every outsourced translation due time, so late returns are followed from one list.

problems.words: Typing errors cause applications to be rejected and redone
quick_ideas: Have a second person check applications for the most common service this week, so errors are caught before submission
List this month's rejections by type once, so you see where errors start.

workzap_build.text: a check step per service before submission, with rejections and rework logged per person and service.

problems.free_stops: the checks per service are worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count which service type causes the most retyping this week, so the error-heavy work is obvious to the team.
Give one staff member the final spelling check on that service before release, so redo work stops eating counter time.

problems.words: Different staff quote different service charges for the same thing
quick_ideas: Write one service charge list and give it to every counter, so customers hear the same price
Display it where customers can see it, so there's no doubt.

workzap_build.text: a standard price list in the system, so every counter charges the same and every receipt matches.

problems.free_stops: how prices and receipts are set up is designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare what each staff member quoted today for the same common service, so price drift across the counter is visible.
Keep one handwritten charge list at one agreed counter spot, so every quote starts from the same source.

problems.words: Cash at the counter doesn't match the day's transactions, and government fees don't reconcile
quick_ideas: Count cash against the day's jobs at close for one week, so you see how often it's out
Keep service charges and government fees in separate totals, so they're not mixed.

workzap_build.text: a daily reconciliation of service charges, government fees paid and counter cash, by counter and branch.

problems.free_stops: how fees and cash are matched is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: For one week, note jobs finished and receipt slips issued at closing, so missed writing or missed handovers stand out.
Keep one counter notebook for unfinished jobs and receipt-slip issues during each shift, so staff can resolve mismatches before customers return.

problems.words: Corporate clients run up balances and pay late
quick_ideas: List each corporate account's balance once, so you know who owes most
Send each a statement this week, so the amount is in front of them.

workzap_build.text: a corporate account ledger with statements and scheduled reminders.

problems.free_stops: the reminder sequence is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each corporate account's oldest unpaid bill beside its balance once, so late payers needing follow-up stand out clearly.
Give one staff member the weekly collections notebook and callback time, so every corporate reminder is tracked in one place.

never_say: Any immigration, visa, legal, labour or attestation-procedure advice, or how to get an approval.
Anything involving forgery, altered documents, fake stamps, backdating or paying officials to speed things up.
That a document will be ready or approved by a certain date.
Requests for customer names, passport, Emirates ID, CNIC, visa or certificate details, or copies of documents.

sample_reply.person: Our phones don't stop. Every customer calls several times asking if their attestation is back. Is there a fix for this?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, there is, and you can start this week. 1) Tell every customer once at the counter when to expect their job back, so status calls drop. 2) Message today the customers whose jobs are already ready, so they come in without calling. Workzap can do this automatically for you: every job tracked by reference number, with a WhatsApp update to the customer, with their permission, at each stage. Would you like me to put together a solution document and quote for you? You're free to say no.
